summary: Defines MIB objects for managing SONET/SDH interfaces. It is a companion to the documents that define managed objects for the other interface types. It is a draft standard.

eli5.summary: SONET is a way to send lots of data over fiber. This memo lists what a manager can look at to see how such a line is doing.

questions: how does snmp monitor sonet interfaces
subtitle: The SNMP objects a manager reads to see how a SONET or SDH optical line is performing.

tldr.problem: Operators need a standard way to monitor and configure SONET/SDH links, which are layered into sections, lines, paths and virtual tributaries, each with its own faults and error counts.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3592 defines a SMIv2 MIB module, SONET-MIB. It shows how each SONET/SDH layer appears as an interface in the ifTable, and defines tables of status, error counters and 15-minute history for each layer, plus far-end counterparts.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 2558, fixing typographical errors and adding larger path widths, and is a Draft Standard.

today: RFC 3592 is a Draft Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It obsoletes RFC 2558, which in turn built on RFC 1595.

sections.title: What the Module Covers
sections.content:
RFC 3592 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing Synchronous Optical Network / Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SONET/SDH) interfaces. It is a companion to the documents that define managed objects for the DS1/E1/DS2/E2 and DS3/E3 interface types.

The objects are used when the medium of an interface is SONET/SDH. They apply to the ifType values sonet (39), sonetPath (50) and sonetVT (51). The definitions rest on ANSI T1.105 and T1.106 and on CCITT G.707, G.708, G.709 and G.783. The module is written in SMIv2 and read through SNMP.
sections.eli5: Fiber lines have a standard set of things worth checking. This memo gives each one a name so every manager looks at the same dials.

sections.title: SONET/SDH Layers as Interfaces
sections.content:
A SONET/SDH port is a stack of layers, and not all equipment terminates all of them. A regenerator terminates Sections only. Add-drop multiplexers and digital cross connect systems terminate Lines. Terminal multiplexers may also terminate Paths and VTs/VCs.

The memo maps the layers onto the interfaces table of RFC 2863. The Physical Medium, Section and Line layers share one ifEntry, with ifType sonet(39). Each Path gets its own ifEntry with sonetPath(50), and each virtual tributary (VT) gets one with sonetVT(51). How they are multiplexed is recorded in the ifStackTable and ifInvStackTable.

For these entries only the ifGeneralInformationGroup needs to be supported. ifOperStatus is down(2) whenever the layer's current status shows any defect. For example, ifSpeed for a line might be 155520000 bps, an STS-1 path is 50112000 bps and a VT1.5 is 1728000 bps.
sections.eli5: A fiber line is like a building: floors stacked on floors. Each floor that matters gets its own entry in the building directory.

sections.title: Defects, Failures and Error Seconds
sections.content:
The memo defines the terms the counters rely on. Coding Violations (CVs) are bit interleaved parity (BIP) errors in the incoming signal. An Errored Second (ES) is a second with one or more CVs or an incoming defect at that layer. A Severely Errored Second (SES) is a second with a threshold number of CVs or an incoming defect. A Severely Errored Framing Second (SEFS) has one or more severely errored frame events and is counted only at the Section layer.

Defects include Loss of Signal, Loss of Frame, Loss of Pointer, Alarm Indication Signal (AIS) and Remote Defect Indication (RDI). A defect usually becomes a failure after persisting for 2.5 +/- 0.5 seconds, and clears after being absent for 10 +/- 0.5 seconds.

SES thresholds differ between standards, so the object sonetSESthresholdSet says which set the agent uses: other, bellcore1991, ansi1993, itu1995 or ansi1997. If it is not implemented, the older RFC 1595 interpretation in Appendix B applies. Changing it invalidates earlier SES statistics.
sections.eli5: An errored second is a second with a mistake. A severely errored second is a second with lots of mistakes. The counters just tally those seconds.

sections.title: Groups and Tables
sections.content:
The module is rooted at sonetMIB under transmission 39. Objects are grouped by layer: Medium, Section, Line, Far End Line, Path, Far End Path, Virtual Tributary and Far End VT. Each layer except Medium has a Current table, covering the current 15 minute interval, and an Interval table with the completed intervals. All are indexed by ifIndex.

The Medium group holds configuration: sonetMediumType (sonet or sdh), line coding (B3ZS, CMI, NRZ, RZ), line type (single mode, multi-mode, coax, UTP), the circuit identifier, and a loopback setting with facility and terminal loopbacks.

Each Current table has a status object that is a bit map, so several defects can be shown at once. For example, the Section status uses 1 for no defect, 2 for LOS and 4 for LOF. Path status adds STS LOP, STS AIS, STS RDI, Unequipped and Signal Label Mismatch. The tables also carry ES, SES, CV and, for lines, paths and VTs, unavailable second (UAS) counters. The Far End tables report the same counts as seen by the remote end.
sections.eli5: Each floor of the building has a status light and tally counters, one set for the current quarter hour and a saved set for past quarter hours.

sections.title: History and Unavailable Time
sections.content:
The Interval tables hold up to the previous 24 hours as 96 completed 15 minute intervals. A system must store at least 4 intervals and the default is 32. sonetMediumValidIntervals reports how many are available.

An interface becomes unavailable at the onset of 10 contiguous SESs, and those 10 seconds count as unavailable time. It becomes available again after 10 contiguous seconds with no SESs, which are excluded. While unavailable, only the UAS count increases. An agent cannot know for 10 seconds which state a second belongs to, so it must either adjust counts retroactively or use the delay-line approach in Appendix A, passing one-second statistics through a 10-element delay line so the counters lag real time by 10 seconds.

Either way, a linkDown trap is sent only once the unavailable state is certain, but carries the time of the first UAS, 10 seconds earlier.
sections.eli5: If the line is badly broken for ten seconds in a row, the counters stop counting mistakes and only count "line was down". The agent waits ten seconds to be sure.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects are read-write: sonetMediumType, sonetMediumLineCoding, sonetMediumLineType, sonetMediumCircuitIdentifier, sonetMediumLoopbackConfig, sonetSESthresholdSet, sonetPathCurrentWidth and sonetVTCurrentWidth. Writing them can disrupt a network, from invalid performance data to interrupted traffic.

The readable objects may also be sensitive, since together they reveal performance and some configuration. The RFC recommends that implementers consider SNMPv3 with its authentication and privacy features. It says that deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Some dials can be turned, and turning them wrongly can break the line. So only the right people should be allowed to touch or even peek at them.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 2558
sections.content:
This memo replaces RFC 2558, and the changes are listed in the module's REVISION clause. It corrects the typo bellcore1991(2) in sonetSESthresholdSet and adds sts192cSTM64(6) and sts768cSTM256(7) to sonetPathCurrentWidth.

It also corrects the description of how VTs apply to SDH, clarifies that CV counts should be frozen during SESs, and fixes two typographical errors in the terminology section.
sections.eli5: This is a corrected second edition: it fixes a few typos and adds names for two newer, faster line sizes.
